transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Rajiv (Redwood CSM), Dr. Mira Kapoor (Concordia CTO), Jordan Ellis (SRE Lead), Priya Sharma (Product)
---
00:00 Liam: All right everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda: safety checklist, telemetry handoff, and pick dates for the dry run.
00:22 Dr. Mira: Sounds good. We have a couple folks pulled in from infra if needed but Jordan will lead the live switch.
00:35 Jordan: Yeah I'm here, I've got the on-call rota open. What's the proposed traffic gating?
00:48 Sofia: Our recommendation is phased activation behind a feature flag — start at 1% for 2 hours, then 10% for 6 hours, 50% over the next day, and then full. We'll include automatic health gates for latency, error rate and model quality regression.
01:10 Priya: Quick Q, how do you measure model quality regressions in production? We want to avoid silent drift.
01:24 Sofia: Good question. We use a lightweight live eval that compares a sampled set of responses against the golden prompt set and basic semantic similarity heuristics. It's not perfect but it catches big regressions. We'll push the eval scores to the telemetry stream.
01:42 Dr. Mira: Any false positive risk where the gate flips and we auto-roll back for a transient spike?
01:50 Liam: We set short cool-downs and require persistent breaches — like three consecutive 5-minute windows — before automated rollback. That's configurable.
02:03 Jordan: Can we get those windows in the runbook? We need explicit thresholds to wire up PagerDuty rules.
02:10 Rajiv: Absolutely, we'll include the exact alert rules and runbook snippets in the handoff doc.
02:22 Dr. Mira: Also we need to ensure logs sent to our SIEM are redacted — PHI/PII is a hard no.
02:33 Sofia: Understood. By default Redwood redacts prompts flagged by the customer-supplied PII list. We also support field-level encryption and KMS integration for log storage.
02:45 Priya: Who's responsible for the PII list? We're still finalizing a set of sensitive prompts.
02:52 Dr. Mira: That's on us — Priya will own it. We'll send the first pass by Monday.
03:00 Priya: Yep will do.
03:10 Liam: OK, on the telemetry side, here's what we'll hand over: token-level latency histograms, prefix-cache hit rates, batching sizes, model instance CPU/GPU utilization, and the live-eval score timeseries. We'll also give Grafana dashboards and synthetic probes.
03:32 Jordan: Do you have sample dashboards we can import?
03:37 Sofia: Yes, link in chat: https://redwood.app/shared/concordia-telemetry-template — it's a templated dashboard that maps to our metrics.
03:50 Jordan: Perfect. I'll import that and map our alerting to PagerDuty.
04:05 Dr. Mira: On the topic of rollback, what are the manual vs automatic rollback criteria?
04:12 Liam: Automatic rollback triggers on sustained SLO breaches or if error rate exceeds 5% over the window. Manual rollback is in the runbook and requires two on-call acknowledgements and a tagged rollback commit.
04:28 Jordan: SLO numbers — what's the baseline we should expect for 95th latency?
04:34 Sofia: On hosted at your typical payloads we saw 95th at ~220ms for short prompts; with caching and batching that slides. For the dedicated capacity numbers we gave in the benchmark deck it's around 120–180ms depending on sequence length. Expect slight variance in prod.
04:56 Priya: Is there a graceful degradation path to a cheaper model variant if load spikes?
05:03 Liam: Yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible smaller model flavor; we can set cost vs latency policies. That was in the model routing section of the SRE playbook.
05:16 Dr. Mira: What about dedicated vs hosted fallback? We are leaning private but want hosted as emergency fallback — is that supported?
05:25 Sofia: It's supported assuming network egress and data residency approvals; our Private control plane can route to Redwood-hosted fallback but logs would still be under your retention policy with encryption. We'll need to coordinate NATS/VPN rules.
05:40 Jordan: Sounds like a network task. I'll open a ticket with our network team to validate peering.
05:48 Rajiv: Can we talk through the dry run plan now? We propose a two-hour dry run where we simulate a 10% to 50% traffic increase and test rollback.
06:02 Priya: Who should be on call for that?
06:05 Jordan: At minimum SRE lead, product owner, Redwood SE and AE, and 24/7 on-call.
06:12 Liam: We'll have Sofia lead the test and Rajiv coordinate communications. Suggested dates: 2025-10-10 or 2025-10-11.
06:25 Dr. Mira: 10th looks good for us. We'll confirm by EOD.
06:33 Jordan: For the telemetry handoff, can Redwood push an example set of anonymized logs so we can validate ingestion?
06:41 Sofia: Yes, we'll export a sanitized sample bucket to the S3 path you provide. Need the S3 ARN and the IAM role.
06:50 Jordan: I'll send the ARN after the call.
07:02 Priya: Security evidence — SOC2 compliance and audit logs — have we gotten those?
07:08 Liam: We shared the high-level SOC2 report and the audit log schema last week. If you need deeper artifacts, our security team can coordinate an NDA and a secure share.
07:20 Dr. Mira: We'll probably need the architecture diagram for the private deployment and the KMS integrations.
07:27 Sofia: We'll attach the private-deployment-arch.pdf to the handoff packet.
07:34 Jordan: A couple of nitpicks: we want retention for the telemetry to be 90 days, and hot access to last 7 days. Can Redwood support tiered retention?
07:45 Rajiv: Yes, tiering is supported. We'll document recommended retention for metrics, traces, and logs.
07:53 Priya: For feature flags and A/B splits, can you show how to roll out by user cohort rather than percent? We want to target only 2 internal teams first.
08:03 Sofia: Absolutely. We can do audience targeting via user attributes or by a list of hashed identifiers. We'll include sample flag configs.
08:16 Dr. Mira: On billing — will alerting on higher than expected token usage create automated throttles?
08:23 Liam: No automated throttles by default. We can set hard quota gates but usually we do notify then throttle only if customer requests. We can discuss quota gates for safety if you prefer.
08:36 Jordan: Let's keep throttle off for the DR run.
08:40 Priya: One more technical: how are you handling KV cache warming on scale-up? Warm-up can add latency spikes.
08:49 Sofia: We pre-warm via a synthetic prefix workload during the rollout windows and keep a small steady-state traffic to maintain cache hits. The runbook includes a warming script.
09:02 Jordan: Excellent.
09:10 Liam: Okay recap of immediate commitments: Redwood will share the telemetry template link (done), sanitized log sample (Sofia), and runbook snippets with alert rules (Rajiv). Concordia will send PII prompt list (Priya), provide S3 ARN and confirm dry-run date (Jordan).
09:30 Dr. Mira: That's a good plan. Anything else?
09:36 Priya: One ask — can Redwood estimate cost delta for routing 50% traffic to hosted fallback for 24 hours? We want a ballpark.
09:44 Liam: We can run a quick cost model based on token estimates; we'll send a spreadsheet by Thursday.
09:52 Rajiv: Action item noted.
10:00 Liam: Great. We'll sync next week same time unless the dry-run is earlier. Thanks everyone.
10:08 Dr. Mira: Thanks all.
---
Auto-summary (may be imperfect): Safety gating plan finalized; telemetry handoff items listed; dry-run tentatively 2025-10-10; action items assigned for telemetry exports, PII list, and SOC2 evidence path.
References and artifacts mentioned: https://redwood.app/shared/concordia-telemetry-template, private-deployment-arch.pdf, benchmark deck (link in CRM).
